paper.title: Variational Quantum Optimization with Continuous Bandits

settings.name_in_paper: Continuous best arm identification for Lipschitz bandits on [0,1] (location accuracy, lower bound)
unmapped: Goal is to output x_hat with |x_hat - x*| <= epsilon w.p. >= 1-delta (accuracy in arm location, not in value); fixed-confidence sample complexity E[tau]
mu is unimodal only locally: unimodal on every interval of length < kappa_0
the learner knows the target accuracy epsilon and confidence delta
settings.definition_quote: we consider a bandit problem $([0,1], M(x))$, which satisfies the following assumptions: (i) The rewards $M(x)$ are $1$-sub-Gaussian. (ii) The expected reward $\mu(x)$ is $L$-Lipschitz. (iii) $\mu(x)$ has a unique optimum $x^*$. (iv) There is a constant $\kappa_0$, such that $\mu$ is unimodal on every set $E \subseteq [x_i, x_i + \kappa]$ for all $\kappa < \kappa_0$. ... $\Pr(\lVert \hat{x} - x^* \rVert_2 > \ep) \leq \delta$.

symbols.c_star: sup over sampling densities w of inf over alternative L-Lipschitz instances lambda (argmax at distance > epsilon) of integral w(x)(mu(x)-lambda(x))^2 dx

conditions: sampling strategies restricted to Riemann-integrable densities

source.label: thm:exact_lower_bound
source.quote: Let $\mu$ be a bandit continuous bandit on some set $\mathcal{X}$. For any $(\ep, \delta)$-PAC learner, \E[\tau_{\delta}^{\ep}] \geq \frac{\log(1/\delta)}{c^*(\mu)}, where c^*(\mu) = \sup_{w \in \mathcal{W}} \inf_{\lambda \in \mathrm{Alt}^{\ep}(\mu)} \int_{\mathcal{X}} w(x) (\mu(x) - \lambda(x))^2 dx.

results.notes: Stated for general domain X; recorded under the 1-d setting.

conditions: alternate set: 1-Lipschitz lambda with max mu - max lambda > epsilon (value-based alternative)

source.label: cor:trivial_lower_bound
source.quote: Let $\mathcal{L}$ be the space of $1$-Lipschitz functions on $\mathcal{X}$ and \mathrm{Alt}^{\ep}(\mu) \triangleq \{\lambda \in \mathcal{L}:\max_x \mu(x) - \max_x \lambda(x) > \ep\}. Then, c^*(\mu) = \ep^{2}.

results.notes: The corollary only states c* = eps^2; combined with Theorem 4.1 this yields E[tau] >= log(1/delta)/eps^2. Paper calls it a weaker instance-independent lower bound.

bound.regime: kappa_0 > epsilon > 0 (proof uses epsilon sufficiently small)

symbols.sum_B: sum_{t=1}^D m(B_t)/8^(D-t), with B_t = v^{-1}(2^{-t}, 2^{-(t-1)}] level sets of the gap function, m Lebesgue measure, D = log2(1/epsilon)

source.label: thm:approx_lower_bound
source.quote: Let $v:[0,1]\rightarrow \RR$ satisfy the assumptions from \Cref{sec:preliminaries}. Then, \E[\tau_{\delta}^{\ep}] \geq \frac{\log(1/\delta)}{80\ep^3/L}\sum_{t=1}^{D}\frac{m(B_t)}{8^{D-t}}.

results.notes: Paper's L is Lipschitz constant L_lip.

symbols.beta_z: zooming dimension of mu (in [0,1] for d=1)

source.label: cor:approx_lower_bound
source.quote: Let $v:[0,1]\rightarrow \RR$ with zooming dimension $\beta$ satisfy the assumptions from \Cref{sec:preliminaries}. Then, \E[\tau_{\delta}^{\ep}] \geq \boldsymbol{\Theta}(\log(1/\delta)\ep^{-2 + \beta}), when $\ep \rightarrow 0$.

results.notes: Exponent recorded as printed (-2+beta); Corollary 3 has -(beta+2) and claims they match, so a sign typo is likely somewhere.

symbols.sum_B: sum_{t=1}^D m(B_t)/8^(D-t), with B_t = v^{-1}(2^{-t}, 2^{-(t-1)}] level sets of the gap function, m Lebesgue measure, D = log2(1/epsilon)

tuning: confidence intervals at level 1 - delta/(|H_t| 2^t) of length 2^{-(t+3)}

source.label: thm:rr_upper_bound
source.quote: Let $v:[0,1]\rightarrow \RR$ satisfy the assumptions from \Cref{sec:preliminaries}. Then~\Cref{alg:rr} terminates after $D\triangleq\log_2(1/\ep)$ rounds and the number of samples is bounded by \tau_{\delta}^{\ep} \leq 2^{15}L\frac{\log_2(1/\ep)+\log(1/\delta)}{\ep^3}\sum_{t=1}^D \frac{m(B_t)}{8^{D-t}}.

results.notes: Theorem does not state probability type; proof bounds samples on the event that all confidence intervals are correct (prob >= 1-delta), so recorded as high probability. Output is epsilon-optimal in value; paper says unimodality not needed for this. Computation linear in number of samples.

symbols.beta_z: zooming dimension of mu (in [0,1] for d=1)

source.label: cor:algo_complexity
source.quote: Consider $v:[0,1]\rightarrow \RR$, which satisfies the assumptions from \Cref{sec:preliminaries} and has \emph{zooming dimension} $\beta$. Then \tau_{\delta}^{\ep} = \mathcal{O}\left((\log{1/\delta} + \log{1/\ep})\ep^{-(\beta + 2)}\right) and when $\ep \rightarrow 0$, $\E[\tau_{\delta}^{\ep}]$ matches the lower bound from~\Cref{cor:approx_lower_bound}.

results.notes: Exponent as printed -(beta+2); the proof writes O(eps^{-2+beta}), inconsistent. Probability type inherited from Theorem 5.1.

cited_results.setting_description: Tree-armed (continuum, zooming dimension beta) bandits; any strategy; regret r_T at round T
